verses.zh: 我们既已得救，才知道那岛名叫马耳他。
verses.en: After we had safely reached shore,[NOTE:1] we learned that the island was called Malta.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “We having been brought safely through” [to land] (same verb as 27:44). The word “shore” is implied, and the slight variations in translation from 27:44 have been made to avoid redundancy in English. The participle διασωθέντες (diasōthentes) has been taken temporally.
For location see JP4-A3.sn Malta is an island (known by the same name today) in the Mediterranean Sea south of Sicily. The ship had traveled 625 mi (1,000 km) in the storm.

verses.zh: 土人看待我们，有非常的情分；因为当时下雨，天气又冷，就生火接待我们众人。
verses.en: The local inhabitants[NOTE:1] showed us extraordinary[NOTE:2] kindness, for they built a fire and welcomed us all because it had started to rain[NOTE:3] and was cold.
notes: Although this is literally βάρβαροι (barbaroi; “foreigners, barbarians”) used for non-Greek or non-Romans, as BDAG 166 s.v. βάρβαρος 2.b notes, “Of the inhabitants of Malta, who apparently spoke in their native language Ac 28:2, 4 (here β. certainly without derogatory tone…).”
BDAG 1019 s.v. τυγχάνω 2.d states, “δυνάμεις οὐ τὰς τυχούσας extraordinary miracles Ac 19:11. Cp. 28:2.”

Or “because it was about to rain.” BDAG 418 s.v. ἐφίστημι 4 states, “διὰ τ. ὑετὸν τὸν ἐφεστῶτα because it had begun to rain Ac 28:2…But the mng. here could also be because it threatened to rain (s. 6).”

verses.zh: 那时，保罗拾起一捆柴，放在火上，有一条毒蛇，因为热了出来，咬住他的手。
verses.en: When Paul had gathered a bundle of brushwood[NOTE:1] and was putting it on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened itself on his hand.
notes: Or “sticks.”

verses.zh: 土人看见那毒蛇悬在他手上，就彼此说：「这人必是个凶手，虽然从海里救上来，天理还不容他活着。」
verses.en: When the local people[NOTE:1] saw the creature hanging from Paul’s[NOTE:2] hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer! Although he has escaped from the sea, Justice herself[NOTE:3] has not allowed him to live!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Although this is literally βάρβαροι (barbaroi; “foreigners, barbarians”) used for non-Greek or non-Romans, as BDAG 166 s.v. βάρβαρος 2.b notes, “Of the inhabitants of Malta, who apparently spoke in their native language Ac 28:2, 4 (here β. certainly without derogatory tone…).”
Grk “his”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

That is, the goddess Justice has not allowed him to live. BDAG 250 s.v. δίκη 2 states, “Justice personified as a deity Ac 28:4”; L&N 12.27, “a goddess who personifies justice in seeking out and punishing the guilty—‘the goddess Justice.’ ἡ δίκη ζῆν οὐκ εἴασεν ‘the goddess Justice would not let him live’ Ac 28:4.” Although a number of modern English translations have rendered δίκη (dikē) “justice,” preferring to use an abstraction, in the original setting it is almost certainly a reference to a pagan deity. In the translation, the noun “justice” was capitalized and the reflexive pronoun “herself” was supplied to make the personification clear. This was considered preferable to supplying a word like ‘goddess’ in connection with δίκη.

The entire scene is played out initially as a kind of oracle from the gods resulting in the judgment of a guilty person (Justice herself has not allowed him to live). Paul’s survival of this incident without ill effects thus spoke volumes about his innocence.

verses.zh: 保罗竟把那毒蛇甩在火里，并没有受伤。
verses.en: However,[NOTE:1] Paul[NOTE:2] shook[NOTE:3] the creature off into the fire and suffered no harm.
notes: BDAG 737 s.v. οὖν 4 indicates the particle has an adversative sense here: “but, however.”
Grk “he”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “shaking the creature off…he suffered no harm.” The participle ἀποτινάξας (apotinaxas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

verses.zh: 土人想他必要肿起来，或是忽然仆倒死了；看了多时，见他无害，就转念，说：「他是个　神。」
verses.en: But they were expecting that he was going to swell up[NOTE:1] or suddenly drop dead. So after they had waited[NOTE:2] a long time and had seen[NOTE:3] nothing unusual happen[NOTE:4] to him, they changed their minds[NOTE:5] and said he was a god.[NOTE:6]
notes: Or “going to burn with fever.” According to BDAG 814 s.v. πίμπρημι, either meaning (“swell up” or “burn with fever”) is possible for Acts 28:6.
The participle προσδοκώντων (prosdokōntōn) has been taken temporally.
The participle θεωρούντων (theōrountōn) has been taken temporally.
Grk “happening.” The participle γινόμενον (ginomenon) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Grk “changing their minds.” The participle μεταβαλόμενοι (metabalomenoi) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
And said he was a god. The reaction is like Acts 14:11-19 where the crowd wanted to make Paul and Barnabas into gods. The providence of God had protected Paul again.

verses.zh: 离那地方不远，有田产是岛长部百流的；他接纳我们，尽情款待三日。
verses.en: Now in the region around that place[NOTE:1] were fields belonging to the chief official[NOTE:2] of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and entertained us hospitably as guests for three days.
notes: BDAG 798 s.v. περί 2.a.γ states, “of nearby places…τὰ περὶ τὸν τὸπον the region around the place Ac 28:7.” The presence of ἐκεῖνον (ekeinon) results in the translation “that place.”

That is, the chief Roman official. Several inscriptions have confirmed the use of πρῶτος (prōtos) as an administrative title used on the island of Malta for the highest Roman official. See further BDAG 852 s.v. Πόπλιος.

verses.zh: 当时，部百流的父亲患热病和痢疾躺着。保罗进去，为他祷告，按手在他身上，治好了他。
verses.en: The father[NOTE:1] of Publius lay sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him[NOTE:2] and after praying, placed[NOTE:3] his hands on him and healed[NOTE:4] him.
notes: Grk “It happened that the father.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.

Grk “to whom Paul going in.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“whom”) was replaced by a personal pronoun (“him”) and a new sentence begun here in the translation. The participle εἰσελθών (eiselthōn) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
The participle ἐπιθείς (epitheis) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
And healed him. Here are healings like Luke 9:40; 10:30; 13:13; Acts 16:23.

verses.zh: 从此，岛上其余的病人也来，得了医治。
verses.en: After this had happened, many of the people on the island who were sick[NOTE:1] also came and were healed.[NOTE:2]
notes: BDAG 142 s.v. ἀσθένεια 1 states, “ἔχειν ἀ. be ill Ac 28:9.”
Many…also came and were healed. Again, here is irony. Paul, though imprisoned, “frees” others of their diseases.

verses.zh: 他们又多方地尊敬我们；到了开船的时候，也把我们所需用的送到船上。
verses.en: They also bestowed many honors,[NOTE:1] and when we were preparing to sail,[NOTE:2] they gave[NOTE:3] us all the supplies we needed.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “they also honored us greatly”; Grk “they also honored us with many honors” (an idiom).

BDAG 62 s.v. ἀνάγω 4, “as a nautical t.t. (ἀ. τὴν ναῦν put a ship to sea), mid. or pass. ἀνάγεσθαι to begin to go by boat, put out to sea.” In this case the simpler English “sail” is more appropriate. The English participle “preparing” has also been supplied, since the provisioning of the ship would take place some time before the actual departure.
BDAG 384 s.v. ἐπιτίθημι 1.b has “give τινί τι someth. to someone…ἀναγομένοις τὰ πρὸς τὰς χρείας when we sailed they gave us what we needed Ac 28:10.”
They gave us all the supplies we needed. What they had lost in the storm and shipwreck was now replaced. Luke describes these pagans very positively.

verses.zh: 过了三个月，我们上了亚历山大的船往前行；这船以「宙斯双子」为记，是在那海岛过了冬的。
verses.en: After three months we put out to sea[NOTE:1] in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island and had the “Heavenly Twins”[NOTE:2] as its figurehead.[NOTE:3]
notes: BDAG 62 s.v. ἀνάγω 4, “as a nautical t.t. (ἀ. τὴν ναῦν put a ship to sea), mid. or pass. ἀνάγεσθαι to begin to go by boat, put out to sea.”

That had the ‘Heavenly Twins’ as its figurehead. The twin brothers Castor and Pollux, known collectively as the Dioscuri or ‘Heavenly Twins,’ were the twin sons of Zeus and Leda according to Greek mythology. The Alexandrian ship on which Paul and his companions sailed from Malta had a carved emblem or figurehead of these figures, and they would have been the patron deities of the vessel. Castor and Pollux were the “gods of navigation.” To see their stars was considered a good omen (Epictetus, Discourses 2.18.29; Lucian of Samosata, The Ship 9).tn Or “the ‘Twin Gods’”; Grk “the Dioscuri” (a joint name for the pagan deities Castor and Pollux).
Or “as its emblem.”

verses.zh: 到了叙拉古，我们停泊三日；
verses.en: We put in[NOTE:1] at Syracuse[NOTE:2] and stayed there three days.
notes: Grk “And putting in.” The participle καταχθέντες (katachthentes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style. On the meaning of the participle, BDAG 516 s.v. κατάγω states, “Hence the pass., in act. sense, of ships and seafarers put in εἴς τι at a harbor…εἰς Συρακούσας Ac 28:12.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
Syracuse was a city on the eastern coast of the island of Sicily. It was 75 mi (120 km) from Malta.

verses.zh: 又从那里绕行，来到利基翁。过了一天，起了南风，第二天就来到部丢利。
verses.en: From there we cast off[NOTE:1] and arrived at Rhegium,[NOTE:2] and after one day a south wind sprang up[NOTE:3] and on the second day we came to Puteoli.[NOTE:4]
notes: A few early mss (א* B Ψ [gig] sa [bo]) read περιελόντες (perielontes, “[From there we] cast off [and arrived at Rhegium]”; cf. Acts 27:40). The other major variant, περιελθόντες (perielthontes, “[we] sailed from place to place”), is found in P74 א2 A 066 1739 M lat sy. Although περιελόντες is minimally attested, it is found in the better witnesses. As well, it is a more difficult reading, for its meaning as a nautical term is uncertain, requiring something like “τὰς ἀγκύρας be supplied = ‘we weighed anchor’” (BDAG 799 s.v. περιαιρέω 1). It thus best explains the rise of the other readings.
Rhegium was a city on the southern tip of Italy. It was 80 mi (130 km) from Syracuse.

Grk “after one day, a south wind springing up, on the second day.” The genitive absolute construction with the participle ἐπιγενομένου (epigenomenou) has been translated as a clause with a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Puteoli was a city on the western coast of Italy south of Rome. It was in the Bay of Naples some 220 mi (350 km) to the north of Rhegium. Here the voyage ended; the rest of the journey was by land.

verses.zh: 在那里遇见弟兄们，请我们与他们同住了七天。这样，我们来到罗马。
verses.en: There[NOTE:1] we found[NOTE:2] some brothers[NOTE:3] and were invited to stay with them seven days. And in this way we came to Rome.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “where.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“where”) has been replaced with the demonstrative pronoun (“there”) and a new sentence begun here in the translation.
Grk “finding.” The participle εὑρόντες (heurontes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
That is, some fellow Christians.
For location see JP4-A1.

verses.zh: 那里的弟兄们一听见我们的信息就出来，到亚比乌市和三馆地方迎接我们。保罗见了他们，就感谢　神，放心壮胆。
verses.en: The brothers from there,[NOTE:1] when they heard about us, came as far as the Forum of Appius[NOTE:2] and Three Taverns[NOTE:3] to meet us. When he saw them,[NOTE:4] Paul thanked God and took courage.
notes: Mention of Christian brothers from there (Rome) shows that God’s message had already spread as far as Italy and the capital of the empire.

The Forum of Appius was a small traveler’s stop on the Appian Way about 43 Roman miles (62 km) south of Rome (BDAG 125 s.v. ᾿Αππίου φόρον). It was described by Horace as “crammed with boatmen and stingy tavernkeepers” (Satires 1.5.3).
Three Taverns was a stop on the Appian Way 33 Roman miles (49 km) south of Rome.

Grk “whom, when he saw [them], Paul.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“whom”) was replaced by the personal pronoun (“them”) and a new sentence begun here in the translation.

verses.zh: 进了罗马城，（有古卷加：百夫长把众囚犯交给御营的统领，惟有）保罗蒙准和一个看守他的兵另住在一处。
verses.en: When we entered Rome, Paul was allowed to live[NOTE:1] by himself, with the soldier who was guarding him.
notes: Or “to stay.”sn Allowed to live by himself. Paul continued to have a generous prison arrangement (cf. Acts 27:3).

verses.zh: 过了三天，保罗请犹太人的首领来。他们来了，就对他们说：「弟兄们，我虽没有做甚么事干犯本国的百姓和我们祖宗的规条，却被锁绑，从耶路撒冷解在罗马人的手里。
verses.en: After three days[NOTE:1] Paul[NOTE:2] called the local Jewish leaders[NOTE:3] together. When they had assembled, he said to them, “Brothers,[NOTE:4] although I had done[NOTE:5] nothing against our people or the customs of our ancestors,[NOTE:6] from Jerusalem[NOTE:7] I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.[NOTE:8]
notes: Grk “It happened that after three days.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
Grk “he”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
L&N 33.309 has “‘after three days, he called the local Jewish leaders together’ Ac 28:17.”
Grk “Men brothers,” but this is both awkward and unnecessary in English.
The participle ποιήσας (poiēsas) has been translated as a concessive adverbial participle.
I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our ancestors. Once again Paul claimed to be faithful to the Jewish people and to the God of Israel.tn Or “forefathers”; Grk “fathers.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Grk “into the hands of the Romans,” but this is redundant when παρεδόθην (paredothēn) has been translated “handed over.”

verses.zh: 他们审问了我，就愿意释放我；因为在我身上，并没有该死的罪。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] they had heard my case,[NOTE:2] they wanted to release me[NOTE:3] because there was no basis for a death sentence[NOTE:4] against me.
notes: Grk “who when.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“who”) has been replaced by the personal pronoun (“they”) and a new sentence begun at this point in the translation.
Or “had questioned me”; or “had examined me.” BDAG 66 s.v. ἀνακρίνω 2 states, “to conduct a judicial hearing, hear a case, question.”
They wanted to release me. See Acts 25:23-27.
Grk “no basis for death,” but in this context a sentence of death is clearly indicated.

verses.zh: 无奈犹太人不服，我不得已，只好上告于凯撒，并非有甚么事要控告我本国的百姓。
verses.en: But when the Jews objected,[NOTE:1] I was forced to appeal to Caesar[NOTE:2]—not that I had some charge to bring[NOTE:3] against my own people.[NOTE:4]
notes: That is, objected to my release.
Or “to the emperor” (“Caesar” is a title for the Roman emperor).

BDAG 533 s.v. κατηγορέω 1 states, “nearly always as legal t.t.: bring charges in court.” L&N 33.427 states for κατηγορέω, “to bring serious charges or accusations against someone, with the possible connotation of a legal or court context—‘to accuse, to bring charges.’”
Or “my own nation.”

verses.zh: 因此，我请你们来见面说话，我原为以色列人所指望的，被这链子捆锁。」
verses.en: So for this reason I have asked to see you and speak with you, for I am bound with this chain because of the hope of Israel.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The hope of Israel. A reference to Israel’s messianic hope. Paul’s preaching was in continuity with this Jewish hope (Acts 1:3; 8:12; 14:22; 19:8; 20:25).

verses.zh: 他们说：「我们并没有接着从犹太来论你的信，也没有弟兄到这里来报给我们说你有甚么不好处。
verses.en: They replied,[NOTE:1] “We have received no letters from Judea about you, nor have any of the brothers come from there[NOTE:2] and reported or said anything bad about you.
notes: Grk “they said to him.”
Or “arrived”; Grk “come” (“from there” is implied). Grk “coming.” The participle παραγενόμενος (paragenomenos) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

verses.zh: 但我们愿意听你的意见如何；因为这教门，我们晓得是到处被毁谤的。」
verses.en: But we would like to hear from you what you think, for regarding this sect we know[NOTE:1] that people[NOTE:2] everywhere speak against[NOTE:3] it.”
notes: Grk “regarding this sect it is known to us.” The passive construction “it is known to us” has been converted to an active one to simplify the translation.
Grk “that everywhere it is spoken against.” To simplify the translation the passive construction “it is spoken against” has been converted to an active one with the subject “people” supplied.
On the term translated “speak against,” see BDAG 89 s.v. ἀντιλέγω 1.

verses.zh: 他们和保罗约定了日子，就有许多人到他的寓处来。保罗从早到晚，对他们讲论这事，证明　神国的道，引摩西的律法和先知的书，以耶稣的事劝勉他们。
verses.en: They set[NOTE:1] a day to meet with him,[NOTE:2] and they came to him where he was staying[NOTE:3] in even greater numbers.[NOTE:4] From morning until evening he explained things[NOTE:5] to them,[NOTE:6] testifying[NOTE:7] about the kingdom of God[NOTE:8] and trying to convince[NOTE:9] them about Jesus from both the law of Moses and the prophets.
notes: Grk “Having set.” The participle ταξάμενοι (taxamenoi) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Grk “Having set a day with him”; the words “to meet” are not in the Greek text, but are implied.
Or “came to him in his rented quarters.”
BDAG 848 s.v. πολύς 1.b.β.ב states, “(even) more πλείονες in even greater numbers Ac 28:23.”
The word “things” is not in the Greek text, but has been supplied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, but must be supplied for the modern English reader.

Grk “to whom he explained.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“whom”) has been replaced by the pronoun (“them”) and a new sentence begun at this point in the translation.
BDAG 233 s.v. διαμαρτύρομαι 1 has “to make a solemn declaration about the truth of someth. testify of, bear witness to (orig. under oath)…God’s kingdom 28:23.”

Testifying about the kingdom of God. The topic is important. Paul’s preaching was about the rule of God and his promise in Jesus. Paul’s text was the Jewish scriptures. This is yet another summary of the message like that in 18:28. The nature of the kingdom of God in the NT and in Jesus’ teaching (along with Paul’s teaching here) has long been debated by interpreters and scholars, with discussion primarily centering around the nature of the kingdom (earthly, heavenly, or both) and the kingdom’s arrival (present, future, or both). An additional major issue concerns the relationship between the kingdom of God and the person and work of Jesus himself. See also Luke 6:20; 11:20; 17:20-21; Acts 1:3.
Or “persuade.”

verses.zh: 他所说的话，有信的，有不信的。
verses.en: Some were convinced[NOTE:1] by what he said,[NOTE:2] but others refused[NOTE:3] to believe.
notes: Or “persuaded.”
Grk “by the things spoken.”
Some were convinced…but others refused to believe. Once again the gospel caused division among Jews, as in earlier chapters of Acts (13:46; 18:6).

verses.zh: 他们彼此不合，就散了；未散以先，保罗说了一句话，说：「圣灵藉先知以赛亚向你们祖宗所说的话是不错的。
verses.en: So they began to leave,[NOTE:1] unable to agree among themselves, after Paul made one last statement: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly to your ancestors[NOTE:2] through the prophet Isaiah
notes: The imperfect verb ἀπελύοντο (apeluonto) has been translated as an ingressive imperfect.
Or “forefathers”; Grk “fathers.”

verses.zh: 他说：你去告诉这百姓说：你们听是要听见，却不明白；看是要看见，却不晓得；
verses.en: when he said,‘Go to this people and say,“You will keep on hearing,[NOTE:1] but will never understand,and you will keep on looking,[NOTE:2] but will never perceive.
notes: Grk “you will hear with hearing” (an idiom).
Or “seeing”; Grk “you will look by looking” (an idiom).

verses.zh: 因为这百姓油蒙了心，耳朵发沉，眼睛闭着；恐怕眼睛看见，耳朵听见，心里明白，回转过来，我就医治他们。
verses.en: For the heart of this people has become dull,[NOTE:1] and their ears are hard of hearing,[NOTE:2] and they have closed their eyes,so that they would not see with their eyesand hear with their earsand understand with their heartand turn,[NOTE:3] and I would heal them.”’[NOTE:4]
notes: The heart of this people has become dull. The charge from Isaiah is like Stephen’s against the Jews of Jerusalem (Acts 7:51-53). They were a hard-hearted and disobedient people.tn Or “insensitive.”
Grk “they hear heavily with their ears” (an idiom for slow comprehension).
Note how the failure to respond to the message of the gospel is seen as a failure to turn.
A quotation from Isa 6:9-10.

verses.zh: 所以你们当知道，　神这救恩，如今传给外邦人，他们也必听受。」（有古卷加：
verses.en: “Therefore be advised[NOTE:1] that this salvation from God[NOTE:2] has been sent to the Gentiles;[NOTE:3] they[NOTE:4] will listen!”[NOTE:5]
notes: Grk “Therefore let it be known to you.”
Or “of God.”
The term Gentiles is in emphatic position in the Greek text of this clause. Once again there is the pattern: Jewish rejection of the gospel leads to an emphasis on Gentile inclusion (Acts 13:44-47).
Grk “they also.”

Some later mss include 28:29: “When he had said these things, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.” Verse 29 is lacking in P74vid א A B E Ψ 048 33 81 1175 1739 2464 and a number of versions. They are included (with a few minor variations) in M it and some versions. This verse is almost certainly not a part of the original text of Acts, as it lacks the best credentials. The present translation follows NA28 in omitting the verse number, a procedure also followed by a number of other modern translations.

verses.zh: 保罗说了这话，犹太人议论纷纷地就走了。）
保罗在自己所租的房子里住了足足两年。凡来见他的人，他全都接待，
verses.en: Paul[NOTE:1] lived[NOTE:2] there two whole years in his own rented quarters[NOTE:3] and welcomed[NOTE:4] all who came to him,
notes: Grk “He”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “stayed.”

Or perhaps, “two whole years at his own expense.” BDAG 654 s.v. μίσθωμα states, “the customary act. mng. ‘contract price, rent’…is not found in our lit. (Ac) and the pass. what is rented, a rented house is a mng. not found outside it (even Ammonius Gramm. [100 ad] p. 93 Valck. knows nothing of it. Hence the transl. at his own expense [NRSV] merits attention) ἐν ἰδίῳ μισθώματι in his own rented lodgings Ac 28:30 (for the idea cf. Jos., Ant. 18, 235).”
Or “and received.”

verses.zh: 放胆传讲　神国的道，将主耶稣基督的事教导人，并没有人禁止。
verses.en: proclaiming the kingdom of God[NOTE:1] and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ[NOTE:2] with complete boldness[NOTE:3] and without restriction.[NOTE:4]
notes: See the note on the kingdom of God in v. 23.
Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”
Or “openness.”

Proclaiming…with complete boldness and without restriction. Once again Paul’s imprisonment is on benevolent terms. The word of God is proclaimed triumphantly and boldly in Rome. Acts ends with this note: Despite all the attempts to stop it, the message goes forth.
